## Framing: options the brief omits
**A. Manual relay** — C3 already builds a pack and ingests a reply file; add pack→clipboard and reply←clipboard and a human carries both. Terms-neutral, no extension, works everywhere, days of work. The brief never considers the human already in the loop.
**B. Read-only extraction** — the user sends; the extension only reads the finished answer into the ledger. Drops `send`/`new_chat`/`attach`; recasts the claim from "automates the site" to "reads the page the user is on"; still feeds ratings.
**C. Sanctioned routes first** — `agy` already covers the Gemini account the brief cites; the new capability is grok.com free. Reclaim Gemini with `agy` before building a browser engine for it.
Unstated and decision-shaping: store or sideload? It decides whether "adapters fetched through the telemetry channel" is legal under MV3 — and what signing can mean.
**Needed to choose:** store vs sideload; does the user accept the "debugger attached" infobar (trusted events need `chrome.debugger`); are prose-only replies acceptable; in-writing acceptance of *account* ban risk per adapter; PowerShell parity or C3 only; real per-site turn quota.

## Q1 — Boundary
Ship nothing site-identifying: no domain in manifest host permissions, no selector, no fixture, no doc naming gemini.google.com or grok.com, empty catalogue. No `cookies` permission, no credential read, no CAPTCHA/anti-bot code, no self-patching selector repair (site logic by another name). Catalogue = signed pointers, never code: `{adapter_id, site_domain, contract_version, semver, sha256, signer_pubkey, fetch_url}`. Signing = publisher keys plus a user-pinned trust set (TOFU); a project CA makes the company the distributor again. Precedent: userscript managers ship and host no scripts; a separate directory (Greasy Fork) lists user code by hash with a disclaimer. gemini-mcp already states it plainly — automated use of the consumer web app is contrary to Google's terms; the program is a personal client for the user's own account. Reuse that sentence in README, licence and the per-adapter consent at enable time.

## Q2 — Shape
Declarative JSON adapter first (selectors, timing, status — data), WASM escape hatch second, in the user's own tab. JSON is hashable and cannot exfiltrate. An outside CDP/Playwright driver is disqualified: profile dir or debug port (credential exposure) and hidden from the user. `chrome.debugger` is the only trusted-event path and its infobar is a feature — the user sees every turn; if refused, accept untrusted JS events knowingly. WASM's real sandbox is the JS host API (the module cannot touch the DOM), so that API is the security artifact: per-tab, DOM read/click/type, no `fetch`, no `chrome.*`, no cross-tab, enforced in the background.
The five verbs carry no identity, no failure class, no completion boundary. Minimum: `id/site/contract_version/dom_signature`; `probe() -> ok|logged_out|rate_limited|gate|dom_changed`; `new_chat()`; `send(text)`; `await_answer(timeout) -> {text, complete}`; `limits() -> {max_input_tokens, max_turns, min_interval_ms, thread_continuable}`. Drop `attach` in v1 — the one verb that invites exfiltration and changes site terms. `complete` matters: a still-streaming or virtualised answer truncates silently.

## Q3 — Detection
Also: hard-stop and retire the adapter version on any gate/limit signal; never auto-dismiss a consent or CAPTCHA-shaped dialog; one site, one tab, strictly sequential (parallel fan-out is a correlated footprint); mandatory per-run token on the loopback WS plus Origin validation — Chrome treats 127.0.0.1 as trustworthy, so any web page can open that socket, and gemini-mcp ships the token off by default; jittered delays; refuse to run unless the tab is visible and focused, which makes "user sees every turn" enforceable; no scheduled runs; never touch site settings; name the user's account risk, not only the product's.

## Q4 — Quality
Make the per-adapter budget a first-class engine bound (C3 already fails "brief too large for this engine"): default ~4–8k tokens, asserted not estimated. Free tiers cap turns, so `-FormatRetry` repair is a second real message: default repair off for `browser`, count every turn against quota and ledger. No repo tools → read-only class, lowest router band until N rated consults, `findings_unavailable` for prose-only. Continue the site thread only when `limits().thread_continuable` and the adapter can name it; else stateless re-send as `http` does; tag with `ConversationTrust`.

## Q5 — Telemetry
`adapter_id`, `adapter_version`, `site_domain`, `contract_version`, `outcome_class` (answered | prose_only | gate | rate_limited | dom_changed | login_required), `turns_used`, `repair_used`. `outcome_class` is what makes retirement computable. Aggregate per `(adapter_id, contract_version)`, or a dead version's score inherits into its successor. Ship an empty catalogue; updates opt-in, user-initiated, hash-verified, landing disabled; the retract list advisory and locally overridable — a remote kill switch is remote control.

## Q6 — Order
(0) Manual relay and a written boundary/refusal policy. (1) A user-written spike on one site: does human-cadence driving survive a week without a gate? If not, the engine is dead and nothing else should be built. (2) Declarative schema, host API, authenticated relay, read-only mode. (3) Telemetry and the per-adapter table. (4) A user-land reference adapter in a separate repo. (5) WASM last. "'`chrome.debugger` is the only trusted-event path and its infobar is a feature - the user sees every turn; if refused, accept untrusted JS events knowingly. Valid JSON, 9 findings, markdown 703 naive-count words (~645 real words). Good.

One concern: the JSON contains `C:\\Users\\...` inside here-string — in a single-quoted here-string, backslashes are literal, so the JSON has `C:\\Users` which parses to `C:\Users`. Correct.

Also `crates\\c3-core\\src\\lineage.rs` → `crates\c3-core\src\lineage.rs`. Good.

Now my final message must be exactly this JSON object. I'll output it verbatim (without the surrounding PowerShell). Note the JSON is one line — fine.

Let me output it exactly as validated.

{"schema_version":"1","verdict":"ADVISE","verdict_reason":"The framing is buildable, but it locks in three choices (a WASM-first adapter model, fetched adapter updates, and a send-driving contract) before the boundary, the distribution channel and the deliverable's value have been decided, and it omits a compliant human-in-the-loop option that may deliver most of the value at no terms risk.","reply_markdown":"## Framing: options not listed
**A** Manual relay: pack->clipboard, reply<-clipboard; a human carries both ways. Covers sites with no adapter; the brief never considers the human already in the loop.
**B** Read-only extraction: the user sends; the extension only reads the answer into the ledger. Drops `send`/`new_chat`/`attach`.
**C** Sanctioned routes first: `agy` already covers the cited Gemini account; the new capability is grok.com free.
**Need:** store or sideload (decides MV3 legality of fetched adapters and signing); acceptance of the 'debugger attached' infobar (trusted input needs `chrome.debugger`); are prose-only replies acceptable; in-writing acceptance of *account* ban risk; PowerShell parity or C3 only; per-site turn quota.
## Q1 - Boundary
Ship nothing site-identifying: no domain in host permissions, no selector, no doc naming a site, empty catalogue. No `cookies` permission, no credential read, no CAPTCHA/anti-bot code, no self-patching selector repair (site logic by another name). Catalogue = signed pointers, never code: `{id, site, contract_version, sha256, signer, url}`. Signing = publisher keys with a user-pinned trust set (TOFU); a project CA makes the company the distributor again. Precedent: userscript managers ship and host no scripts; directories list user code by hash only. gemini-mcp already says it: automated use of the consumer web app is contrary to Google's terms; the program is a personal client for the user's own account. Reuse it in README, licence and per-adapter consent.
## Q2 - Shape
Declarative JSON adapter first (selectors, timing, status - data), WASM second, in the user's own tab: JSON is hashable and cannot exfiltrate. Disqualified: an outside CDP/Playwright driver - profile dir or debug port means credential exposure, hidden from the user. `chrome.debugger` is the only trusted-event path; its infobar shows the user every turn. WASM's real sandbox is the JS host API (the module cannot touch the DOM), so that API is the artifact: per-tab, DOM read/click/type, no `fetch`, no `chrome.*`, no cross-tab.
The five verbs carry no identity, failure class or completion boundary. Minimum: `id/site/contract_version/dom_signature`; `probe() -> ok|logged_out|rate_limited|gate|dom_changed`; `new_chat()`; `send(text)`; `await_answer(timeout) -> {text, complete}`; `limits() -> {max_input_tokens, max_turns, min_interval_ms, thread_continuable}`. Drop `attach` in v1; `complete` catches a truncated read.
## Q3 - Detection
Also: hard-stop and retire the adapter version on any gate or limit signal; never auto-dismiss a CAPTCHA-shaped dialog; one site, one tab, strictly sequential (parallel fan-out is a correlated footprint); mandatory per-run token and Origin check on the loopback WS (127.0.0.1 is treated as trustworthy, so any page can open it; gemini-mcp ships the token off); jittered delays; refuse to run unless the tab is visible and focused, making 'user sees every turn' enforceable; no scheduled runs; name the user's account risk, not just the product's.
## Q4 - Quality
Make the per-adapter budget a first-class engine bound (C3 already fails 'brief too large for this engine'): default ~4-8k tokens, asserted not estimated. Free tiers cap turns, so `-FormatRetry` repair is a second real message - default repair off for `browser`, every turn counted against quota and ledger. No repo tools means read-only class, lowest router band until N rated consults, `findings_unavailable` for prose-only. Continue the site thread only when `limits().thread_continuable` and the adapter can name it; else stateless re-send as `http` does.
## Q5 - Telemetry
`adapter_id`, `adapter_version`, `site_domain`, `contract_version`, `outcome_class` (answered | prose_only | gate | rate_limited | dom_changed | login_required), `turns_used`, `repair_used`. `outcome_class` makes retirement computable. Aggregate per `(adapter_id, contract_version)`, else a dead version's score inherits into its successor. Ship an empty catalogue; updates opt-in, user-initiated, hash-verified, landing disabled; the retract list advisory, locally overridable - a remote kill switch is remote control.
## Q6 - Order
(0) Manual relay plus a written boundary/refusal policy. (1) A user-written spike on one site: does human-cadence driving survive a week without a gate? If not, build nothing else. (2) Declarative schema, host API, authenticated relay, read-only mode. (3) Telemetry and the per-adapter table. (4) A user-land reference adapter in a separate repo. (5) WASM last. Do not build: any adapter here; runtime-fetched code; stealth; CAPTCHA handling; `attach`; scheduling; panel fan-out; PowerShell parity.
